subject.title: [Feature]: SSRF 内网访问确认机制

question: Should OpenClaw add browser private-network SSRF confirmation or allow/block policy in core, and which security semantics should ship first?
rationale: The request changes browser egress controls and public config/CLI behavior; automation can verify the missing surface but cannot choose the safe approval UX, metadata override policy, or compatibility contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve staged policy first
options.body: Define explicit allow/block semantics, non-overridable metadata behavior, audit output, docs, and tests before considering interactive prompts.

options.title: Approve interactive confirmation now
options.body: Commit to a user approval UX with timeout, rate limiting, session scoping, and navigation/redirect coverage across browser paths.

options.title: Keep current strict model
options.body: Continue with strict default plus host exceptions and document broad private-network access as a trusted-environment opt-in only.

recommendation.title: Approve staged policy first
recommendation.body: Define explicit allow/block semantics, non-overridable metadata behavior, audit output, docs, and tests before considering interactive prompts.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has the strongest recent merged-history signal around browser config/docs and SSRF policy surfaces that this decision would extend.
